To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
selenocystelyl–tRNA synthetase forms a supramolecular decamer ring assembly, which does not exist in the presence of its substrate, tRNAsec.
bacterial selenocys-tein synthase (Sel) is a homodimeric protein that binds one tRNAsec per subunit and can form supramolecular complexes of stacked decameric rings.
bacterial selenocys-teine synthase (a selenoprotein) forms a decamer assembly with tRNAsec (a non-selenoprotein).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function of the bacterial selenocys-teine synthetase SelA.
the structure and function of the bacterial selenocytine synthase SelA and the assembly of SelA with its substrate tRNAsec.
the assembly and structure of bacterial selenoprotein synthesis machinery and the role of the SelA–SelB–SelC (tRNA(sec)) complex in the synthesis of selenocysteinyl-tRNA(sec).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SelA decamer is the functional unit of selenocysteinyl-tRNA synthetase in bacteria.
SelA is a homodimer in solution and in the presence of selenocystely–tRNAsec.
SelA is a homodimer, but the SelA–SelA–SelA complex is the catalytically active form of this enzyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SelA–tRNAsec is a dimer in solution and a tetramer in the crystal, and that it forms decameric rings of dimers in the presence of SelC.
the bacterial selenocys-teine synthase (bSelA) forms an oligomeric assembly in solution, which is composed of stacked decameric rings.
SelA forms a supramolecular assembly of decamer rings in which tRNAsec binds in a 1:1 stoichiometry.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the bacterial selenocytsteine synthase–SelC assembly is not an obligate 2:2 heterodimer as previously proposed, but a monomer–SelC complex, which can form supramolecular complexes in the absence of tRNAsec.
the bacterial selenocyssteine synthase (selenocysteyltRNA synthetase) has a 1:1 binding stoichiometry with its tRNA.
the stoichiometry of the SelA–SelC assembly is 1:1 rather than 1:2 as previously proposed.
